grounds. (a) The corpus is a **census, not a sample** — `tasks/**/plans/v*.md`
is the entire population of committed plans at ship time, so "exactly 3, zero
FPs" is a population statement about everything the check will retroactively
see, not an out-of-sample precision estimate; the only unmeasured population is
FUTURE plans, and no held-out slice of the current corpus represents those
better than the corpus does. (b) Acceptance criterion 4's load-bearing role is
**transcription-drift detection**, not precision measurement — §8 risk 1 says
so explicitly ("shipped regexes drift from the calibrated prototype →
different corpus counts") — and re-scanning the calibration corpus is exactly
the right instrument for that. (c) The generalization claim is deliberately
weak: WARN-class advisory, §12.12 tags the forecast "Medium", §4's blind-spot

snapshots", and kill criterion 1 pre-registers the response to a future
confirmed FP. The plan already frames the number as calibration fit (the D1
comment is headed "CORPUS CALIBRATION", snapshot-dated). No remedy required.

but never states as such: the arming vocabulary is **house vocabulary, not
#2221's idiolect** — the third `_C69_ARM_RE` alternate ("re-generate … at ≥2×")
matches the CLAUDE.md registration shape every compliant plan quotes when
arming the trigger, so recall on future plans is anchored to the standing
rule's wording, not one document. Constructed misses the grammar cannot catch:
*"the cap-hit re-generation pass is enabled, doubling the cap for flagged
rows"* (no armed/arming/auto-fires token; verbal multiplier "doubling" is not

silent-inheritance case (a follow-up arming the parent's trigger without
restating it — no vocabulary at all). All three are false negatives. For a
WARN-class advisory whose blind-spot enumeration already names "recall on
future arming phrasings outside the calibrated grammar" as uncertified, that is
an acceptable posture — critics remain the semantic arbiters.

**Q3 — criteria quantitative and evaluable.** Yes: all six acceptance criteria
and three kill criteria are measurable as written, at implement time, by the
implementer (criterion 4 names both harness and actor; §8 rows 1–2 restate it).
